newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ staff fear 1000 jobs may go-paper.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ staff fear 1000 jobs may go-paper.

text.p: Air New Zealand staff fear more than 1,000 jobs may be slashed by the airline in its bid to cut costs by about NZ$100 million, the Christchurch Press reported on Wednesday.
Several divisions within the company, including some providing ground services, were likely to be sold to independent contractors as part of "Project Save".

Already on the block were the catering centres in Christchurch, Wellington, Auckland and Rarotonga. Their 500 employees faced an uncertain future as seven companies, four of them based overseas, considered their purchase.

"New Zealanders were told when Brierley bought the airline that it would stay in New Zealand's hands, but it now seems it's going to be sold off bit by bit to overseas interests," said Neil Hammond, assistant regional secretary of the Service Workers' Union.

Brierley Investments Ltd owns 42.5 percent of Air New Zealand, with 55 percent of its 'A' shares, which must remain under New Zealand control, and 30 percent of its 'B' shares, which can be owned by anyone.

Hammond declined to named the parties interested in the catering division, but The Press said sources had identified Canadian-based company Cater Air, which is partly owned by Qantas, as a top contender.
Qantas holds 19.9 percent of Air New Zealand.
"Most employees right through the company from the top to the bottom are deeply concerned about the future of their jobs," Hammond said.

The Press said no one knew, or was prepared to reveal, when an announcement on the impact of Project Save would be made, but one insider believed it would not be before the carrier's half-year financial results were reported on February 19.
The effects of the cuts were likely to be felt across the board, including within subsidiaries such as the Mount Cook Group.
Some ground facilities such as reservations, check-in, and engineering services could be merged into the parent company's operations.
The paper said Air New Zealand had refused to comment on the union's concerns. An Air New Zealand spokesman told Reuters the company would not comment on a speculative story.
Air New Zealand owns half of Ansett Australia.
